facts.name: Employee Eligibility Scope
facts.sentence: This insurance certificate applies to employees of Global Constructors International.

facts.name: Expatriate Employee Coverage
facts.sentence: Coverage includes employees working on international assignments ('Expatriate Employees').

facts.name: Global Roaming Coverage Inclusion
facts.sentence: Coverage also includes employees who regularly travel internationally for business ('Global Roaming Employees').

facts.name: Worldwide Coverage Scope
facts.sentence: The insurance coverage follows the employee worldwide.

facts.name: No Geographical Restrictions
facts.sentence: There are no geographical restrictions on coverage unless specified in Section 7 (Exclusions).

facts.name: Buyback Riders Modify Coverage
facts.sentence: Coverage may be modified by the Buyback Riders.

facts.name: Worldwide Coverage Scope
facts.sentence: Coverage is designed to follow the employee worldwide.

facts.name: No Geographic Restrictions
facts.sentence: There is no restriction on geographic location for coverage.

facts.name: No Geographic Restrictions Beyond Exclusions
facts.sentence: Geographic restrictions on coverage exist only as specifically stated in Section 7 (Exclusions).

facts.name: Buyback Riders Modify Limits
facts.sentence: The Buyback Riders in Section 6 modify coverage limitations.

facts.name: Premium Currency
facts.sentence: Premiums are denominated in U.S. dollars.

facts.name: Dollar Denomination of Benefits
facts.sentence: Benefits are denominated in U.S. dollars.

facts.name: Claim Payment Currency
facts.sentence: Claims are payable in U.S. dollars.

facts.name: Foreign Currency Payment Option
facts.sentence: Payment in foreign currency may be arranged by request.

facts.name: Texas Jurisdiction Clause
facts.sentence: The Master Policy is governed by the laws of Texas.

facts.name: ICC Arbitration Resolution
facts.sentence: International disputes may be resolved by ICC arbitration.

facts.name: ICC Arbitration Option
facts.sentence: ICC arbitration is available at the employer's election.

facts.name: Expatriate Employee Definition
facts.sentence: Expatriate employees are U.S. nationals or legal permanent residents.

facts.name: Expatriate Assignment Status
facts.sentence: Expatriate employees are assigned outside the United States.

facts.name: Expatriate Assignment Duration
facts.sentence: Expatriate employees' assignments are expected to last six months or more.

facts.name: Expatriate Employee Class
facts.sentence: Expatriate employees fall under this certificate’s class.

facts.name: U.S.-Based Business Travelers
facts.sentence: Global Roaming Employees are employees based in the U.S.

facts.name: Global Roaming Employee Definition
facts.sentence: Global Roaming Employees spend more than ninety days per year outside the U.S. on business travel.

facts.name: Basic Coverage Only
facts.sentence: Global Roaming Employees are eligible for basic coverage only.

facts.name: Separate Certificate Class
facts.sentence: Basic coverage for Global Roaming Employees is offered under a separate certificate class.

facts.name: Local National Definition
facts.sentence: Local National Employees are citizens of host countries.

facts.name: Local National Employment Status
facts.sentence: Local National Employees are employed locally.

facts.name: Eligibility Exclusion: Local Nationals
facts.sentence: Local National Employees are not eligible under this policy.

facts.name: Coverage Start Date Trigger
facts.sentence: Coverage commences on the first day of an approved international assignment.

facts.name: Coverage Activation Condition
facts.sentence: Coverage begins when the employee is actively at work.

facts.name: Coverage Commencement Condition
facts.sentence: Coverage begins only when all EOI requirements are satisfied.

facts.name: No EOI Required for $500K Basic Coverage
facts.sentence: Basic coverage up to five hundred thousand U.S. dollars does not require Evidence of Insurability (EOI).

facts.name: EOI Requirement Above $500K
facts.sentence: Coverage exceeding five hundred thousand U.S. dollars requires Evidence of Insurability (EOI).

facts.name: Voluntary Supplemental EOI Requirement
facts.sentence: Any voluntary supplemental election requires Evidence of Insurability (EOI).

facts.name: Basic Life Benefit Calculation
facts.sentence: Basic Life benefit equals three times the annual base salary in U.S. dollars.

facts.name: Benefit Rounding Rule
facts.sentence: Basic Life benefit is rounded to the next higher one thousand U.S. dollars.

facts.name: Base Salary Only
facts.sentence: Basic Life includes base salary only.

facts.name: Housing Allowances Excluded
facts.sentence: Housing allowances are excluded from Basic Life calculation.

facts.name: COLA Excluded from Basic Life
facts.sentence: Cost-of-living adjustments (COLA) are excluded from Basic Life calculation.

facts.name: Hardship Premium Exclusion
facts.sentence: Hardship premiums are excluded from Basic Life calculation.

facts.name: Voluntary Supplemental Increments
facts.sentence: Voluntary Supplemental coverage is available in increments of fifty thousand U.S. dollars.

facts.name: Max Voluntary Supplemental Limit
facts.sentence: Maximum Voluntary Supplemental coverage is five hundred thousand U.S. dollars.

facts.name: Max Voluntary Supplemental Limit
facts.sentence: Maximum Voluntary Supplemental coverage is four times the employee's salary.

facts.name: Voluntary Supplemental Cap
facts.sentence: The lesser amount between five hundred thousand U.S. dollars and four times the salary determines the upper limit for Voluntary Supplemental coverage.

facts.name: Voluntary Supplemental EOI Requirement
facts.sentence: Evidence of Insurability (EOI) is required for Voluntary Supplemental coverage.

facts.name: Supplemental Insurance Increments
facts.sentence: Voluntary Supplemental life insurance is available in increments of $50,000.

facts.name: Voluntary Supplemental Max Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum amount of Voluntary Supplemental life insurance is $500,000.

facts.name: Voluntary Supplemental Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum amount of Voluntary Supplemental life insurance is also limited to four times the employee’s annual salary.

facts.name: EOI Requirement Above $200K
facts.sentence: An Employee Offer Inquiry (EOI) is required for Voluntary Supplemental life insurance amounts exceeding $200,000.

facts.name: Annual Recalculation Date
facts.sentence: Benefit recalculations occur annually on February 1.

facts.name: Annual Salary-Based Recalculations
facts.sentence: Annual benefit recalculations are based on the employee’s salary as of January 1.

facts.name: Maximum Total Coverage Limit
facts.sentence: The total maximum life insurance coverage, including both Basic and Supplemental benefits, is capped at $2,000,000.

facts.name: Rider Benefits Included in Cap
facts.sentence: Rider benefits are included within the $2,000,000 total cap.

facts.name: Hardship Location Coverage Increase
facts.sentence: Basic life coverage is automatically increased by one times the employee’s salary when assigned to a Hardship Level 3 location.

facts.name: Hardship Location Coverage Increase
facts.sentence: Basic life coverage is automatically increased by one times the employee’s salary when assigned to a Hardship Level 4 location.

facts.name: Hardship Location Definition
facts.sentence: Hardship Level 3 and 4 locations are defined according to the current Hardship Schedule maintained by Human Resources.

facts.name: Hardship Assignment Coverage Duration
facts.sentence: The increase in basic life coverage due to hardship assignment applies only during the period of assignment in such a location.

facts.name: Repatriation Benefit Eligibility
facts.sentence: If an employee dies while on assignment outside the United States, Transoceanic will pay a Repatriation Benefit.

facts.name: Repatriation Benefit Maximum
facts.sentence: The Repatriation Benefit can be up to $25,000.

facts.name: Repatriation Remains Transport
facts.sentence: The Repatriation Benefit covers preparation and transportation of remains to the United States or the employee's designated home country.

facts.name: Repatriation Family Travel Coverage
facts.sentence: The Repatriation Benefit includes airfare for one immediate family member to accompany the remains.

facts.name: Repatriation Cost Coverage
facts.sentence: The Repatriation Benefit covers local administrative and documentation costs related to repatriation.

facts.name: Repatriation Payment Process
facts.sentence: The Repatriation Benefit is paid directly to the employer or funeral home upon submission of receipts.

facts.name: Lump Sum Payment Option
facts.sentence: If receipts are not submitted, the Repatriation Benefit may be paid as a flat $15,000 lump sum.

facts.name: Repatriation Benefit Exemption
facts.sentence: The Repatriation Benefit is not subject to beneficiary designation.

facts.name: Repatriation Benefit Exclusion
facts.sentence: The Repatriation Benefit is not part of the standard death benefit.

facts.name: Repatriation Certificate Termination
facts.sentence: When an expatriate employee is repatriated to U.S.-based employment, this life insurance certificate terminates.

facts.name: Coverage Transition Post-Repatriation
facts.sentence: Coverage transitions to the employer's U.S. domestic group life plan, if applicable.

facts.name: Repatriation Coverage Transition
facts.sentence: Transition to the U.S. domestic group life plan occurs on the first day of U.S. employment.

facts.name: No Coverage Gap on Transition
facts.sentence: No coverage gap exists between the end of the expatriate policy and the start of the domestic plan.

facts.name: U.S. Employment Coverage Transition
facts.sentence: Coverage transitions to the employer's U.S. domestic group life plan on the first day of U.S. employment.

facts.name: Seamless Coverage Transition
facts.sentence: No coverage gap occurs when coverage transitions to the employer's U.S. domestic group life plan.

facts.name: Employee Portability Coverage
facts.sentence: If the employee leaves the company, portability of life coverage is available.

facts.name: Portability Coverage Continuation
facts.sentence: Portability allows continuation of basic and supplemental life coverage as direct-pay.

facts.name: Portability Duration Limit
facts.sentence: Portable coverage duration is up to 24 months.

facts.name: Portable Coverage Limit
facts.sentence: Maximum amount of portable coverage is $500,000.

facts.name: Portability Without EOI
facts.sentence: Evidence of Insurability (EOI) is not required for portability.

facts.name: Post-Portability Conversion Option
facts.sentence: After the 24-month portability period, the employee may convert to an individual policy.

facts.name: No EOI for Conversion
facts.sentence: Conversion to an individual policy requires no Evidence of Insurability (EOI).

facts.name: War & Terrorism Coverage Active
facts.sentence: The War and Terrorism Buyback Rider was elected.

facts.name: War & Terrorism Rider Effect
facts.sentence: By electing the War and Terrorism Buyback Rider, the War and Terrorism Exclusion is removed.

facts.name: War Death Benefit Coverage
facts.sentence: Death benefits under the War and Terrorism Buyback Rider are payable for deaths caused by declared or undeclared war.

facts.name: War & Terrorism Coverage
facts.sentence: Death benefits under the War and Terrorism Buyback Rider are payable for deaths caused by acts of terrorism as defined by the U.S. State Department.

facts.name: War and Terrorism Coverage: Civil War
facts.sentence: Death benefits under the War and Terrorism Buyback Rider are payable for deaths caused by civil war.

facts.name: War & Terrorism Coverage: Insurrection
facts.sentence: Death benefits under the War and Terrorism Buyback Rider are payable for deaths caused by insurrection.

facts.name: War & Terrorism Coverage
facts.sentence: Death benefits under the War and Terrorism Buyback Rider are payable for deaths caused by political violence.

facts.name: War & Terrorism Coverage
facts.sentence: Death benefits under the War and Terrorism Buyback Rider are payable for deaths caused by military action by any government.

facts.name: Combatant Death Exclusion
facts.sentence: The War and Terrorism Buyback Rider does not cover death occurring while serving as a combatant in any military force.

facts.name: Aviation Buyback Rider Active
facts.sentence: The Aviation Exclusion Buyback Rider was elected.

facts.name: Aviation Exclusion Removal
facts.sentence: By electing the Aviation Exclusion Buyback Rider, the Aviation Exclusion for non-scheduled private aircraft is removed.

facts.name: Aviation Death Benefit Coverage
facts.sentence: Death benefits under the Aviation Exclusion Buyback Rider are payable for death resulting from operation of or travel in private aircraft.

facts.name: Aviation Coverage for Charter Travel
facts.sentence: Death benefits under the Aviation Exclusion Buyback Rider are payable for death resulting from travel in charter aircraft.

facts.name: Aviation Buyback Coverage Scope
facts.sentence: Death benefits under the Aviation Exclusion Buyback Rider are payable for death resulting from travel in private or charter aircraft anywhere in the world.

facts.name: Aviation Rider Limitations
facts.sentence: The Aviation Exclusion Buyback Rider does not cover death as a pilot or crew member of a military aircraft.

facts.name: Annual Rider Renewal
facts.sentence: Riders are renewable annually during open enrollment.

facts.name: Rider Removal Reinstates Exclusion
facts.sentence: Removal of a rider reinstates the applicable exclusion prospectively.

facts.name: 24-Month Contestability Period Start
facts.sentence: The effective date of coverage or reinstatement determines the start point for a 24-month period.

facts.name: War Death Benefit Exclusion
facts.sentence: If the War/Terror Buyback Rider is not in force, no death benefit is payable for deaths caused by war.

facts.name: No Terrorism Benefit Without Rider
facts.sentence: If the War/Terror Buyback Rider is not in force, no death benefit is payable for deaths caused by acts of terrorism.

facts.name: No Death Benefit for Civil Insurrection
facts.sentence: If the War/Terror Buyback Rider is not in force, no death benefit is payable for deaths caused by civil insurrection.

facts.name: Aviation Death Benefit Exclusion
facts.sentence: If the Aviation Buyback Rider is not in force, no benefit is payable for death occurring while operating a non-scheduled private aircraft.

facts.name: Aviation Exclusion Without Rider
facts.sentence: If the Aviation Buyback Rider is not in force, no benefit is payable for death occurring while traveling as a passenger in a non-scheduled private aircraft.

facts.name: Aviation Exclusion Exception
facts.sentence: Excluded from the aviation exclusion is commercial scheduled airline service.

facts.name: Incontestability Clause
facts.sentence: After 24 months of continuous coverage, Transoceanic cannot deny a claim based on application misrepresentation.

facts.name: Post-contestability fraud exception
facts.sentence: After 24 months of continuous coverage, Transoceanic can still deny a claim based on fraud.

facts.name: No Pre-Existing Condition Exclusion
facts.sentence: There is no pre-existing condition exclusion in the policy.

facts.name: No Hazardous Activity Exclusion
facts.sentence: There is no exclusion for hazardous occupational activities in the policy.

facts.name: No Exclusion for Work at Height
facts.sentence: Work at height is considered a hazardous occupational activity but is not excluded under the policy.

facts.name: No Exclusion for Offshore Work
facts.sentence: Offshore platform work is considered a hazardous occupational activity but is not excluded under the policy.

facts.name: No Exclusion for Confined Spaces
facts.sentence: Working in confined spaces is considered a hazardous occupational activity but is not excluded under the policy.

facts.name: Hazardous Work Coverage
facts.sentence: Working in seismic zones is considered a hazardous occupational activity but is not excluded under the policy.

facts.name: Accelerated Death Benefit Limit
facts.sentence: An employee may accelerate up to 75% of their total life coverage amount.

facts.name: Terminal Illness Certification
facts.sentence: Acceleration of benefits requires certification of terminal illness.

facts.name: Terminal Illness Definition
facts.sentence: Terminal illness is defined as having a life expectancy of 12 months or less.

facts.name: Maximum Accelerated Benefit
facts.sentence: The maximum accelerated death benefit amount is $500,000.

facts.name: Minimum Accelerated Benefit
facts.sentence: The minimum accelerated death benefit amount is $10,000.

facts.name: Acceleration Request Certification
facts.sentence: For employees on international assignment, an acceleration request must include physician certification.

facts.name: Assignment Physician Certification Requirement
facts.sentence: Physician certification for employees on assignment must come from a licensed physician in the employee’s current country of assignment.

facts.name: Physician Certification Flexibility
facts.sentence: Physician certification for employees on assignment may also come from a licensed physician in the United States.

facts.name: Actuarial Discount Basis
facts.sentence: The actuarial discount applied to the accelerated death benefit is based on the current U.S. 6-month T-bill rate.

facts.name: Actuarial Discount Formula
facts.sentence: The actuarial discount includes an additional 150 basis points above the U.S. 6-month T-bill rate.

facts.name: Premium Waiver for Disability
facts.sentence: If an employee becomes totally disabled during an international assignment, premiums are waived.

facts.name: Total Disability Definition
facts.sentence: Total disability is defined according to the employer's long-term disability plan definition.

facts.name: 6-Month Elimination Period
facts.sentence: A 6-month elimination period applies before premium waiver begins.

facts.name: Premium Waiver After Disability
facts.sentence: Premiums are waived after the 6-month elimination period for eligible employees who become totally disabled.

facts.name: Overseas Disability Certification Exception
facts.sentence: For overseas disabilities, the employer's occupational physician may provide certification instead of an independent U.S. physician.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Duration
facts.sentence: The waiver of premiums continues until age 65 unless the employee recovers.

facts.name: Waiver Ends at Age 65
facts.sentence: The waiver of premiums ends when the employee reaches age 65.

facts.name: Waiver Ends on Recovery
facts.sentence: The waiver of premiums ends upon recovery from total disability.

facts.name: Elimination Period Applies
facts.sentence: The elimination period applies to disability benefits.

facts.name: Overseas Disability Certification
facts.sentence: For overseas disabilities, the employer's occupational physician may certify disability status instead of requiring an independent U.S. physician.

facts.name: Waiver Duration Conditions
facts.sentence: A waiver of coverage continues until age 65 or until recovery occurs.

facts.name: Update Beneficiary Designations
facts.sentence: Beneficiary designations must be updated via the employer's global HR platform.

facts.name: Beneficiary Change Effective Date
facts.sentence: Changes to beneficiary designations become effective once acknowledged by Transoceanic.

facts.name: Death Claim Documentation Requirement
facts.sentence: For claims resulting from deaths outside the United States, an authenticated death certificate is required.

facts.name: Apostille Requirement for Hague Members
facts.sentence: An apostille is required on the death certificate when the country involved is a member of the Hague Convention.

facts.name: Consular Report Requirement
facts.sentence: A U.S. consular report of death is required if applicable for claims involving non-U.S. deaths.

facts.name: Global Claim Form Requirement
facts.sentence: A completed Transoceanic global claim form is required for claims arising from deaths outside the U.S.

facts.name: Beneficiary Identity Requirement
facts.sentence: Proof of beneficiary identity is required for claims arising from deaths outside the U.S.

facts.name: Global Claims Hotline Access
facts.sentence: Transoceanic offers a 24/7 global claims hotline for handling international claims.

facts.name: Claims Hotline Contact
facts.sentence: The phone number for the U.S. claims hotline is 1-800-555-8800.

facts.name: Global Claims Hotline Access
facts.sentence: International callers can reach the claims hotline using a collect call at +1-713-555-8800.

facts.name: Global Claims Email Address
facts.sentence: Email correspondence for global claims should be sent to globalclaims@transoceaniclife.com.

facts.name: Claim Processing Timeline
facts.sentence: Claims are processed and paid within 15 business days after receiving complete documentation.

facts.name: No-cost international wire transfers
facts.sentence: International wire transfers are available for claim payments at no additional cost.

facts.name: Expedited Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: Expedited payment processing takes five business days.

facts.name: Expedited Payment Requirements
facts.sentence: Expedited payment requires submission of all necessary documentation along with a $100 review fee.

facts.name: Expedited Fee Waiver for High-Hardship Claims
facts.sentence: The $100 expedited review fee is waived for Hardship Level 3 and Hardship Level 4 assignment claims.

facts.name: Governing Law Jurisdiction
facts.sentence: This insurance certificate is subject to the laws of the State of Texas.

facts.name: Headquarters Location
facts.sentence: Transoceanic Life Insurance Company is headquartered in Houston, Texas.

facts.name: Certificate Issuance Authority
facts.sentence: The President of the International Group Benefits division signed this certificate.

facts.name: Certificate Issuance Date
facts.sentence: This certificate was issued on February 1, 2024.

facts.sentence: All rights and obligations related to the insurance are governed by the Group Master Policy.

facts.sentence: In case of any conflict between this certificate and the Group Master Policy, the Group Master Policy takes precedence.

facts.name: Certificate Not Contract
facts.sentence: This certificate is not a contract of insurance.

facts.name: Evidence of Participation
facts.sentence: This certificate is evidence of the employee’s participation in the group insurance plan.

facts.name: Full-Time Eligibility Criteria
facts.sentence: Active full-time employees who are scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week are eligible for coverage.

facts.name: 60-Day Waiting Period
facts.sentence: Eligible full-time employees must complete a 60-day waiting period from the date of hire before becoming covered.

facts.name: Part-Time Eligibility Limitation
facts.sentence: Part-time employees working between 20 and 29 hours per week are eligible for basic coverage only.

facts.name: Part-Time Benefit Eligibility
facts.sentence: Part-time employees receive half the standard benefit applicable to their salary band.

facts.name: Voluntary Enrollment Deadline
facts.sentence: Enrollment in voluntary supplemental coverage must occur within 45 days of the date of eligibility.

facts.name: Enrollment Requirement: Evidence of Insurability
facts.sentence: Evidence of insurability is required to enroll in voluntary supplemental coverage.

facts.name: Half-Benefit Eligibility Rule
facts.sentence: Employees who become eligible during a pay period are eligible for basic coverage only at one-half the standard benefit applicable to their salary band.

facts.name: Enrollment Window for Supplemental Coverage
facts.sentence: Voluntary supplemental coverage requires enrollment within 45 days of the date of eligibility without evidence of insurability.

facts.name: Late Enrollment EOI Requirement
facts.sentence: Enrollment in voluntary supplemental coverage after 45 days requires satisfactory Evidence of Insurability (EOI) approved by the insurer.

facts.name: Coverage Effective Timing
facts.sentence: Coverage becomes effective on the first day of the calendar month coinciding with or next following the end of the waiting period.

facts.name: Effective Date Employment Requirement
facts.sentence: Coverage becomes effective only if the employee is actively at work on the effective date.

facts.name: Salary-Based Life Insurance Calculation
facts.sentence: Basic life insurance is determined by salary bands based on annual base earnings.

facts.name: Basic Benefit for Low-Income Employees
facts.sentence: For employees earning up to $30,000 annually, the basic benefit is $30,000.

facts.name: Basic Benefit for $30K–$40K Earners
facts.sentence: For employees earning between $30,001 and $40,000 annually, the basic benefit is $50,000.

facts.name: Basic Benefit for $40K–$70K Earners
facts.sentence: For employees earning between $40,001 and $70,000 annually, the basic benefit is $75,000.

facts.name: Basic Benefit for $70K–$100K Earners
facts.sentence: For employees earning between $70,001 and $100,000 annually, the basic benefit is $100,000.

facts.name: Basic Benefit for High Earners
facts.sentence: For employees earning over $100,000 annually, the basic benefit is $150,000.

facts.name: Annual Band Reclassification
facts.sentence: Band reclassification occurs on January 1 of each year based on prior-year W-2 earnings.

facts.name: Mid-Year Salary Changes No Re-Classification
facts.sentence: Mid-year salary changes do not trigger band reclassification.

facts.name: Supplemental Coverage Increments
facts.sentence: Voluntary supplemental coverage is available in increments of $10,000.

facts.name: Maximum Supplemental Coverage Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum voluntary supplemental coverage is $200,000.

facts.name: Max Supplemental Coverage Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum voluntary supplemental coverage is also limited to three times the annual salary.

facts.name: Voluntary Supplemental Cap Rule
facts.sentence: The lesser of $200,000 or three times the annual salary determines the upper limit for voluntary supplemental coverage.

facts.name: EOI Requirement Above $100K
facts.sentence: Evidence of Insurability (EOI) is required for voluntary supplemental coverage above $100,000.

facts.name: AD&D Equals Basic Life Benefit
facts.sentence: The Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) benefit equals the basic life benefit amount for accidental death.

facts.name: Dismemberment Payment Criteria
facts.sentence: Loss of both hands or both feet results in a dismemberment payment equal to 100% of the AD&D benefit.

facts.name: Dismemberment Payment for Hand/Foot Loss
facts.sentence: Loss of one hand and one foot results in a dismemberment payment equal to 100% of the AD&D benefit.

facts.name: AD&D Eye Loss Payout
facts.sentence: Loss of sight of both eyes results in a dismemberment payment equal to 100% of the AD&D benefit.

facts.name: Double Hand Loss Benefit
facts.sentence: Loss of both hands results in 100% of AD&D benefit.

facts.name: Loss of Both Feet Payout
facts.sentence: Loss of both feet results in 100% of AD&D benefit.

facts.name: One Hand One Foot Loss Benefit
facts.sentence: Loss of one hand and one foot results in 100% of AD&D benefit.

facts.name: Double Eye Sight Loss Benefit
facts.sentence: Loss of sight of both eyes results in 100% of AD&D benefit.

facts.name: Partial Disability Payout
facts.sentence: Loss of one hand results in 50% of AD&D benefit.

facts.name: One Foot Loss Benefit
facts.sentence: Loss of one foot results in 50% of AD&D benefit.

facts.name: Loss of One Eye Benefit
facts.sentence: Loss of sight of one eye results in 50% of AD&D benefit.

facts.name: Finger Loss Compensation
facts.sentence: Loss of thumb and index finger on the same hand results in 25% of AD&D benefit.

facts.name: AD&D Supplemental Benefit
facts.sentence: AD&D benefits are payable in addition to the life benefit for accidental death.

facts.name: AD&D Payment Cap
facts.sentence: Total AD&D payments will not exceed 100% of the AD&D benefit per occurrence.

facts.name: Termination via Master Policy End
facts.sentence: Coverage terminates upon termination of the Master Policy.

facts.name: Employment End Date Termination
facts.sentence: Coverage terminates on the last day of the month in which employment ends.

facts.name: Eligibility-based termination
facts.sentence: Coverage terminates when the employee is no longer in an eligible class.

facts.name: Voluntary Cancellation Termination
facts.sentence: Coverage terminates when voluntary coverage is voluntarily cancelled.

facts.name: Last Premium Payment Termination
facts.sentence: Coverage terminates on the last day premium is paid for voluntary coverage.

facts.name: Grace Period for Layoffs
facts.sentence: A 31-day grace period applies to involuntary termination due to layoff.

facts.name: Grace Period Continuation
facts.sentence: Basic coverage remains in force during the 31-day grace period without premium payment.

facts.name: Life Coverage Portability
facts.sentence: Portability of basic and supplemental life coverage combined is allowed upon termination of employment.

facts.name: Portability Application Deadline
facts.sentence: Application for portability must be submitted within 31 days of termination.

facts.name: Max Portable Life Amount
facts.sentence: Maximum portable amount for life coverage is $300,000.

facts.name: Portable Policy Premium Rates
facts.sentence: Premiums for portable policies are based on attained-age group rates.

facts.name: Portability Without Medical Exam
facts.sentence: No evidence of insurability is required for portability.

facts.name: Post-Employment Life Insurance Conversion
facts.sentence: Conversion to an individual whole-life policy is permitted within 31 days of termination.

facts.name: No Evidence Required for Conversion
facts.sentence: Conversion to an individual whole-life policy does not require evidence of insurability.

facts.name: AD&D Not Convertible
facts.sentence: The AD&D rider is not eligible for conversion.

facts.name: AD&D Portability Prohibited
facts.sentence: AD&D coverage cannot be ported upon termination of employment.

facts.name: No AD&D Conversion Allowed
facts.sentence: AD&D coverage cannot be converted upon termination of employment.

facts.name: AD&D Termination on Employment End
facts.sentence: AD&D coverage terminates with the end of group employment.

facts.name: AD&D Conversion Not Allowed
facts.sentence: Conversion of AD&D coverage is not available.

facts.name: Conversion After Termination
facts.sentence: An employee who is terminated may convert their coverage within 31 days of termination.

facts.name: Conversion Eligibility Condition
facts.sentence: Conversion is only possible if there is no evidence of uninsurability.

facts.name: AD&D Rider Non-Portability
facts.sentence: The AD&D rider cannot be ported or converted.

facts.name: AD&D Termination on Employment End
facts.sentence: AD&D coverage terminates when group employment ends.

facts.name: Terminal Illness Benefit Request
facts.sentence: An employee may request acceleration of the death benefit if they have been certified by a licensed physician as having a terminal illness.

facts.name: Terminal Illness Definition
facts.sentence: A terminal illness is defined as having a life expectancy of 24 months or less.

facts.name: Max Acceleration Limit
facts.sentence: Maximum acceleration of the death benefit is limited to 50% of the combined life benefit.

facts.name: Combined Life Benefit Inclusion
facts.sentence: The combined life benefit includes both basic and voluntary life coverage.

facts.name: Maximum Acceleration Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum amount that can be accelerated is $150,000.

facts.name: Actuarial Discount for Accelerated Benefit
facts.sentence: Acceleration is subject to an actuarial present-value discount.

facts.name: Actuarial Discount Formula
facts.sentence: The actuarial present-value discount uses the current treasury rate plus 100 basis points.

facts.name: Death Benefit Reduction
facts.sentence: Accelerating the death benefit reduces the death benefit payable to beneficiaries dollar-for-dollar.

facts.name: AD&D Not Eligible for Acceleration
facts.sentence: The AD&D benefit is not eligible for acceleration under any circumstances.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Period
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if death occurs due to suicide within 24 months of the effective date of coverage.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Window
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if death occurs due to suicide within 24 months of the date of last increase in voluntary coverage.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Regardless of Mental State
facts.sentence: Suicide is excluded regardless of mental state—whether sane or insane.

facts.name: AD&D Suicide Exclusion
facts.sentence: The AD&D benefit is not payable if the loss results from suicide.

facts.name: AD&D Exclusion: Self-Injury
facts.sentence: The AD&D benefit is not payable if the loss results from intentional self-inflicted injury.

facts.name: AD&D War Exclusion
facts.sentence: The AD&D benefit is not payable if the loss results from war or act of war, declared or undeclared.

facts.name: AD&D Exclusion: Military Service
facts.sentence: The AD&D benefit is not payable if the loss results from active military service.

facts.name: AD&D Felony Exclusion
facts.sentence: The AD&D benefit is not payable if the loss results from participation in a felony.

facts.name: AD&D Exclusion: Intoxicated Vehicle Operation
facts.sentence: The AD&D benefit is not payable if the loss results from operating a vehicle while legally intoxicated.

facts.name: AD&D Exclusion: Illness & Medical Treatment
facts.sentence: The AD&D benefit is not payable if the loss results from illness, disease, bacterial infection, or medical treatment thereof, except for infections resulting from an accidental cut or wound.

facts.name: AD&D Exclusion: Unauthorized Substance Use
facts.sentence: The AD&D benefit is not payable if the loss results from voluntary use of any narcotic, drug, or hallucinogen not prescribed by a licensed physician.

facts.name: No Pre-Existing Condition Limitation
facts.sentence: There is no pre-existing condition limitation applied to basic life coverage.

facts.name: No Pre-Existing Condition Limitations
facts.sentence: There is no pre-existing condition limitation applied to supplemental life coverage.

facts.name: No Pre-Existing Condition Limitation
facts.sentence: No pre-existing condition limitation applies to basic life coverage.

facts.name: Supplemental Coverage Exemption
facts.sentence: No pre-existing condition limitation applies to supplemental life coverage.

facts.name: Premium Waiver for Disability
facts.sentence: A premium waiver is available for basic life coverage upon proof of total disability beginning before age 65.

facts.name: Premium Waiver for Voluntary Coverage
facts.sentence: A premium waiver is available for voluntary life coverage upon proof of total disability beginning before age 65.

facts.name: Nine-Month Elimination Period
facts.sentence: The elimination period for premium waiver is nine months.

facts.name: Definition of Total Disability
facts.sentence: Total disability means complete inability to perform any occupation for which the employee is reasonably qualified by education, training, or experience.

facts.name: Annual Disability Verification Requirement
facts.sentence: Annual proof of continuing disability is required for continued premium waiver.

facts.name: Physician Examination Right
facts.sentence: Summit reserves the right to require examination by a physician of its choosing at its own expense.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Termination on Recovery
facts.sentence: Waiver of premiums terminates upon recovery.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Termination on Return to Work
facts.sentence: Waiver of premiums terminates upon return to work in any capacity.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Ends at Age 70
facts.sentence: Waiver of premiums terminates upon attainment of age 70.

facts.name: Beneficiary Change Access
facts.sentence: Beneficiaries can be designated or changed at any time via the employer's HR portal.

facts.name: Beneficiary Change Effective Date
facts.sentence: Changes to beneficiary designation take effect upon receipt by the plan administrator.

facts.name: Beneficiary Succession Rule
facts.sentence: If the primary beneficiary predeceases the insured, benefits pass to the contingent beneficiary.

facts.name: Estate Payout Rule
facts.sentence: If no beneficiary survives the insured, benefits are paid to the estate.

facts.name: Irrevocable Beneficiary Consent Rule
facts.sentence: For irrevocable beneficiary designations, the consent of the irrevocable beneficiary is required for any change.

facts.name: Death Notification Deadline
facts.sentence: Claimants must notify Summit Life & Casualty within 90 days of the insured's death.

facts.name: AD&D Claim Notification Deadline
facts.sentence: Claimants must notify Summit Life & Casualty within 90 days of a qualifying accidental death and dismemberment (AD&D) event.

facts.name: Claim Form Requirement
facts.sentence: A completed claim form is required for submission (available at summitlifeclaims.com).

facts.name: Death Certificate Requirement
facts.sentence: A certified death certificate is required for life claims.

facts.name: Physician Statement Requirement
facts.sentence: An attending physician's statement is required for AD&D claims.

facts.name: Police Report Requirement for AD&D
facts.sentence: A police or accident report is required for AD&D claims if applicable.

facts.name: Beneficiary Verification Requirement
facts.sentence: Proof of beneficiary identity and relationship is required.

facts.name: Claim Submission Address
facts.sentence: Claims should be submitted to Summit Life & Casualty – Group Claims.

facts.name: Claim Submission Address
facts.sentence: The mailing address for submissions is 800 Commerce Blvd., Columbus, OH 43215.

facts.name: Claims Contact Number
facts.sentence: The toll-free phone number for claims inquiries is 1-800-555-7742.

facts.name: Claims Office Location
facts.sentence: Casualty – Group Claims is located at 800 Commerce Blvd., Columbus, OH 43215.

facts.name: Contact Information
facts.sentence: Casualty – Group Claims can be reached via toll-free number: 1-800-555-7742.

facts.name: Claim Acknowledgment Timeline
facts.sentence: 10.4 Summit will acknowledge receipt of a claim within 5 business days of receiving complete documentation.

facts.name: Claim Decision Timeline
facts.sentence: 10.4 Summit will render a decision on a claim within 15 business days of receiving complete documentation.

facts.name: Governing Law Clause
facts.sentence: This insurance certificate is governed by the laws of the State of Ohio.

facts.name: Headquarters Location
facts.sentence: Summit Life & Casualty Company is headquartered in Columbus, Ohio.

facts.name: Certificate Signed by SVPI
facts.sentence: The Senior Vice President, Group Insurance signed this certificate.

facts.name: Certificate Issuance Date
facts.sentence: This certificate was issued on January 1, 2024.

facts.name: Defined Terms Reference
facts.sentence: Capitalized terms used in this certificate have definitions specified in Section 12 (Definitions).

facts.name: Eligibility Criteria for Employees
facts.sentence: Eligible employees include active, full-time hourly employees who work 35 or more hours per week.

facts.name: Eligibility Criteria for Salaried Employees
facts.sentence: Eligible employees include active, full-time salaried employees who work 35 or more hours per week.

facts.name: Coverage Effective Timing
facts.sentence: Coverage begins on the first day of the calendar month following 90 days of employment.

facts.name: Eligibility Criteria
facts.sentence: All active, full-time hourly employees regularly working 35 or more hours per week are eligible for coverage.

facts.name: Eligibility Criteria
facts.sentence: All active, full-time salaried employees regularly working 35 or more hours per week are eligible for coverage.

facts.name: Eligibility Start Date
facts.sentence: Coverage for eligible employees begins on the first day of the calendar month following 90 days of continuous service.

facts.name: Spouse Coverage Start Date
facts.sentence: A legal spouse is eligible for dependent life coverage from the same date as the employee.

facts.name: Domestic Partner Eligibility
facts.sentence: A domestic partner registered under applicable state law is eligible for dependent life coverage from the same date as the employee.

facts.name: Spouse Dual-Employee Ineligibility
facts.sentence: A spouse who is also an employee covered under this plan is not eligible for dependent spouse coverage.

facts.name: Child Dependent Eligibility
facts.sentence: Unmarried dependent children from live birth are eligible for dependent life coverage.

facts.name: Child Dependent Eligibility
facts.sentence: Unmarried dependent children from 14 days of age are eligible for dependent life coverage.

facts.name: Eligibility for Adopted Children
facts.sentence: Eligible children include legally adopted children.

facts.name: Stepchildren Eligibility
facts.sentence: Eligible children include stepchildren living in the employee’s household.

facts.name: Child Eligibility Until 26
facts.sentence: Children remain eligible until age 26.

facts.name: Child Dependent Coverage End
facts.sentence: Dependent child coverage ends at age 26.

facts.name: No EOI for Initial Basic Life
facts.sentence: Basic employee life coverage requires no Evidence of Insurability (EOI) when elected within 31 days of eligibility.

facts.name: No EOI for Initial Dependent Coverage
facts.sentence: Initial dependent coverage requires no Evidence of Insurability (EOI) when elected within 31 days of eligibility.

facts.name: Supplemental Coverage EOI Requirement
facts.sentence: Voluntary employee supplemental coverage exceeding $50,000 requires Evidence of Insurability (EOI).

facts.name: Spouse EOI Requirement Over $10K
facts.sentence: Spouse coverage exceeding $10,000 requires Evidence of Insurability (EOI) if enrolled after the initial 31-day period.

facts.name: Late Entrant EOI Requirement
facts.sentence: Any coverage elected by a Late Entrant requires Evidence of Insurability (EOI).

facts.name: Basic Life Coverage Amount
facts.sentence: Employee basic life coverage amount is $50,000 flat for all eligible employees.

facts.name: Basic Life Coverage Uniformity
facts.sentence: Employee basic life coverage does not vary based on salary.

facts.name: Basic Life Coverage Uniformity
facts.sentence: Employee basic life coverage does not vary based on position.

facts.name: Basic Life Coverage Constancy
facts.sentence: Employee basic life coverage does not vary based on tenure.

facts.name: Voluntary Supplemental Coverage Increments
facts.sentence: Employee voluntary supplemental life coverage is available in $25,000 increments.

facts.name: Max Employee Supplemental Coverage
facts.sentence: Maximum employee voluntary supplemental life coverage is $300,000.

facts.name: Voluntary Supplemental Coverage EOI Requirement
facts.sentence: Amounts of employee voluntary supplemental life coverage above $100,000 require Evidence of Insurability (EOI).

facts.name: Max Employee Life Coverage Limit
facts.sentence: Maximum total employee life coverage is $350,000.

facts.name: Spouse Dependent Life Benefit
facts.sentence: Spouse dependent life coverage amount is $25,000 flat.

facts.name: Spouse Coverage Limit Rule
facts.sentence: Spouse dependent life coverage cannot exceed 100% of the employee's total life coverage in force.

facts.name: Child Dependent Life Coverage ($1,000)
facts.sentence: Child dependent life coverage for ages 14 days through 6 months is $1,000.

facts.name: Child Dependent Life Coverage Amount
facts.sentence: Child dependent life coverage for ages 6 months through age 26 is $10,000.

facts.name: Child Benefit: 14 Days–6 Months
facts.sentence: A child aged 14 days through 6 months receives a dependent life benefit of $1,000.

facts.name: Child Benefit Amount
facts.sentence: A child aged 6 months through age 26 receives a dependent life benefit of $10,000.

facts.name: Per-Child Benefit Coverage
facts.sentence: The child benefit is a per-child amount that covers all eligible children.

facts.name: Single Premium Coverage
facts.sentence: The child benefit is provided for a single monthly premium.

facts.name: Age 65 Benefit Reduction
facts.sentence: Employee coverage reduces to 65% of in-force benefit when the employee reaches age 65.

facts.name: Age 70 Coverage Reduction
facts.sentence: Employee coverage reduces to 50% of in-force benefit when the employee reaches age 70.

facts.name: Dependents Not Subject to Age Reduction
facts.sentence: Dependent coverage is not subject to age reduction.

facts.name: Coverage End: Master Policy Termination
facts.sentence: Employee coverage ends on the earliest of: termination of the Master Policy.

facts.name: Employment End Coverage Termination
facts.sentence: Employee coverage ends on the earliest of: the last day of the month employment terminates.

facts.name: Employee Eligibility End
facts.sentence: Employee coverage ends on the earliest of: the date the employee is no longer in an eligible class.

facts.name: Failure to Pay Premiums
facts.sentence: Employee coverage ends on the earliest of: failure to pay required premiums for voluntary coverage.

facts.name: Dependent Coverage End Condition
facts.sentence: Dependent coverage ends on the earliest of: the date employee coverage ends.

facts.name: Eligibility-Based Termination
facts.sentence: Dependent coverage ends on the earliest of: the date the dependent no longer meets the definition of eligible dependent.

facts.name: Dependent Coverage Cancellation
facts.sentence: Dependent coverage ends on the earliest of: the date dependent coverage is cancelled.

facts.name: Spouse Eligibility via Marriage
facts.sentence: Eligible dependents include spouses who remain married.

facts.name: Spouse Coverage Ends After Divorce
facts.sentence: Spouse coverage ends due to divorce or annulment.

facts.name: Child Coverage End at Age 26
facts.sentence: Child coverage terminates at the end of the policy month in which the child attains age 26.

facts.name: Child Coverage Ends on Marriage
facts.sentence: Child coverage terminates at the end of the policy month in which the child gets married.

facts.name: Child Coverage Termination Criteria
facts.sentence: Child coverage terminates at the end of the policy month in which the child otherwise ceases to qualify.

facts.name: Child Coverage Termination Rules
facts.sentence: Child coverage termination occurs at the earliest of: attainment of age 26, marriage, or cessation of qualification.

facts.name: Employee Conversion Privilege
facts.sentence: An employee may convert to an individual whole-life policy without evidence of insurability upon termination of all or part of group life coverage.

facts.name: Employee Conversion Right
facts.sentence: An employee may convert to an individual universal-life policy without evidence of insurability upon termination of all or part of group life coverage.

facts.name: Employee Conversion Window
facts.sentence: Conversion from employee group life coverage requires submission within 31 days of termination.

facts.name: Employee Conversion Limit
facts.sentence: Maximum convertible amount for employee conversion is $250,000.

facts.name: Dependent Conversion Without EOI
facts.sentence: A covered dependent may convert to an individual policy without evidence of insurability upon termination of dependent life coverage.

facts.name: Dependent Conversion Window
facts.sentence: Dependent conversion must occur within 31 days of termination of dependent life coverage.

facts.name: Spouse Conversion Signature Requirement
facts.sentence: For spouse dependent conversion, the application must be signed by the employee.

facts.name: Dependent Conversion Eligibility
facts.sentence: If the dependent is age 18 or older, they may sign their own application for conversion.

facts.name: Dependent Conversion Right
facts.sentence: The covered dependent may convert to an individual policy within 31 days without evidence of insurability.

facts.name: Application Required for Conversion
facts.sentence: Conversion from group coverage to an individual policy requires an application.

facts.name: Spouse Conversion Signature Requirement
facts.sentence: The application for conversion must be signed by the employee when converting on behalf of a spouse.

facts.name: Dependent Signature Requirement
facts.sentence: The application for conversion must be signed by the dependent if the dependent is aged 18 or older.

facts.name: No Portability Option
facts.sentence: Portability is not available under this plan.

facts.name: Termination Continuation Option
facts.sentence: Conversion is the sole continuation option upon termination of employment.

facts.name: FMLA Leave Continuation
facts.sentence: Coverage may continue during approved FMLA leave for up to 12 weeks.

facts.name: FMLA Leave Premium Payment Rule
facts.sentence: Continuation of coverage during approved FMLA leave requires the employee to pay the employee-share premiums directly.

facts.name: No Default AD&D Rider
facts.sentence: This plan does not include an Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) rider by default.

facts.name: AD&D Rider Election via Open Enrollment
facts.sentence: Employees may elect a separate AD&D rider through open enrollment.

facts.name: AD&D Rider Reference
facts.sentence: If an AD&D rider is elected, employees should refer to the AD&D Rider Addendum for details.

facts.name: Chronic Illness Benefit Access
facts.sentence: The Chronic Illness Rider allows acceleration of up to 25% of the employee life benefit per calendar year.

facts.name: Chronic Illness Benefit Minimum
facts.sentence: Acceleration under the Chronic Illness Rider is subject to a $10,000 annual minimum.

facts.name: Chronic Illness Certification Requirement
facts.sentence: To qualify for chronic illness acceleration, the employee must be certified by two independent licensed physicians.

facts.name: Chronic Illness Qualification Criteria
facts.sentence: Chronic illness qualification includes being unable to perform 2 of 6 Activities of Daily Living for 90 consecutive days or more.

facts.name: Dependents Excluded from Acceleration
facts.sentence: Dependent life benefits are not eligible for acceleration under the Accelerated Death Benefit provision.

facts.name: Reduced Death Benefit
facts.sentence: Accelerated benefits reduce the death benefit that would otherwise be paid to beneficiaries.

facts.name: Tax Consequences of Acceleration
facts.sentence: Accelerated benefits may result in tax consequences.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Window
facts.sentence: No benefit is payable for death by suicide within 12 months of the employee's effective date of basic coverage.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion: Supplemental Coverage
facts.sentence: No benefit is payable for death by suicide within 12 months of the employee's effective date of supplemental coverage.

facts.name: Suicide Benefit Exclusion Post-Increase
facts.sentence: No benefit is payable for death by suicide within 12 months of any increase in voluntary coverage.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Limit on Increase
facts.sentence: For suicide-related exclusion related to increased voluntary coverage, the limitation applies only to the amount of the increase.

facts.name: Suicide Benefit Exclusion
facts.sentence: No benefit is provided for death by suicide within 12 months of the employee's effective date of basic or supplemental coverage.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Post-Increase
facts.sentence: No benefit is provided for death by suicide within 12 months of any increase in voluntary coverage.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion on Coverage Increase
facts.sentence: For increases in voluntary coverage, the exclusion applies only to the amount of the increase.

facts.name: Dependent Suicide Exclusion
facts.sentence: No benefit is provided for dependent death by suicide within 12 months of the dependent's effective date.

facts.name: War Death Exclusion
facts.sentence: No benefit is payable for death resulting from a declared war.

facts.name: War Exclusion Clause
facts.sentence: No benefit is payable for death resulting from an undeclared war.

facts.name: Insurrection Death Exclusion
facts.sentence: No benefit is payable for death resulting from insurrection.

facts.name: Military Service Death Exclusion
facts.sentence: No benefit is payable for death resulting from service in the armed forces of any nation.

facts.name: Military Service Benefit Exception
facts.sentence: A benefit may be payable for death resulting from military service if the employee is in the National Guard or Reserve and activated for domestic disaster relief.

facts.name: No Pre-Existing Condition Limitation
facts.sentence: No pre-existing condition limitation applies to employee coverage.

facts.name: Dependent Coverage Without Pre-Existing Limits
facts.sentence: No pre-existing condition limitation applies to dependent coverage.

facts.name: Premium Waiver for Disability
facts.sentence: Employee basic life coverage premiums are waived upon proof of total disability.

facts.name: Voluntary Premium Waiver on Disability
facts.sentence: Employee voluntary life coverage premiums are waived upon proof of total disability.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Eligibility Age
facts.sentence: Proof of total disability must be submitted prior to age 60 to qualify for premium waiver.

facts.name: 6-Month Elimination Period
facts.sentence: A 6-month elimination period applies before the premium waiver begins.

facts.name: Total Disability Definition
facts.sentence: Total disability is defined as complete inability to engage in the employee's own occupation for the first 24 months.

facts.name: Post-24-Month Total Disability Definition
facts.sentence: After the initial 24 months, total disability is defined as complete inability to engage in any gainful occupation.

facts.name: Dependent Premium Waiver During Disability
facts.sentence: Dependent coverage premiums are waived during a period of approved employee disability waiver.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Termination Age
facts.sentence: Waiver of premiums terminates at age 65.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Termination Upon Recovery
facts.sentence: Waiver of premiums terminates upon earlier recovery from disability.

facts.name: Employee Beneficiary Designation
facts.sentence: Beneficiaries for employee life coverage are designated by the employee.

facts.name: Dependent Beneficiary Rule
facts.sentence: Beneficiary for dependent life coverage is the employee, unless the employee predeceases the dependent.

facts.name: Claim Reporting Deadline
facts.sentence: Claims must be reported within 60 days of death.

facts.name: Claim Documentation Requirements
facts.sentence: Required documents for a claim include a certified death certificate.

facts.name: Claim Documentation Requirements
facts.sentence: Required documents for a claim include a completed claim form.

facts.name: Claim Documentation Requirements
facts.sentence: Required documents for a claim include proof of beneficiary identity.

facts.name: Claim Submission Location
facts.sentence: Claims must be submitted to Heartland Mutual Life – Claims Division.

facts.name: Claims Mailing Address
facts.sentence: The mailing address for claims submissions is 500 Meridian Street, Indianapolis, IN 46204.

facts.name: Claims Contact Information
facts.sentence: The claims phone line number is 1-877-555-4600.

facts.name: Claims Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: Heartland will pay valid claims within 10 business days of receiving complete documentation.

facts.name: Headquarters Location
facts.sentence: Heartland Mutual Life Insurance Company is headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana.

facts.name: Certificate Issuance Date
facts.sentence: The certificate is issued on April 1, 2024.

facts.name: Governing Law Clause
facts.sentence: The certificate is governed by the laws of the State of Indiana.

facts.name: Claim Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: Heartland will pay valid claims within 10 business days of complete documentation.

facts.name: Claim Submission via Phone
facts.sentence: Claims can be submitted via phone line: 1-877-555-4600.

facts.name: Definition of Active Employment
facts.sentence: 'Active Employment' means performing regular duties at the employer's place of business or an approved remote location.

facts.name: Definition of Dependent
facts.sentence: 'Dependent' means an eligible spouse or child as defined in Section 2.

facts.name: Late Enrollee Definition
facts.sentence: 'Late Entrant' means an employee or dependent who failed to enroll within the initial eligibility period.

facts.name: Definition of Total Disability
facts.sentence: 'Total Disability' has the meaning set forth in Section 9.2.

facts.name: Certificate Signing Authority
facts.sentence: The President and Chief Operating Officer of Heartland Mutual Life Insurance Company signed the certificate.

facts.name: Plan Enrollment Confirmation
facts.sentence: This certificate evidences participation in FinServ Capital Group's Executive Group Term Life Plan.

facts.name: Non-Qualified Carve-Out Plan
facts.sentence: FinServ Capital Group's Executive Group Term Life Plan is a non-qualified carve-out plan.

facts.name: Class A Executive Coverage
facts.sentence: The plan covers Class A executives.

facts.name: Group Policy Maintenance
facts.sentence: Coverage is maintained under a group term master policy.

facts.name: Supplemental Coverage Structure
facts.sentence: The coverage is supplemental to basic group coverage provided to all employees.

facts.name: Basic Group Coverage Plan
facts.sentence: Basic group coverage is provided under Plan No. PLAC-2024-FS-BASIC.

facts.name: Split-Dollar Death Benefit Allocation
facts.sentence: A split-dollar endorsement arrangement divides the death benefit between the employer and the insured’s designated beneficiary.

facts.name: Split-Dollar Arrangement Reference
facts.sentence: The split-dollar endorsement arrangement is attached as Exhibit A.

facts.name: Exhibit Incorporation by Reference
facts.sentence: Exhibit A is incorporated into this certificate by reference.

facts.name: Non-ERISA Exemption Status
facts.sentence: This plan is not subject to ERISA regulations.

facts.name: Top-Hat Plan Classification
facts.sentence: This plan qualifies as a 'top-hat' plan.

facts.name: Top-Hat Plan Classification
facts.sentence: The top-hat plan is maintained for a select group of management or highly compensated employees.

facts.name: Eligibility via Designation
facts.sentence: Participation in the plan is limited to employees who are designated.

facts.name: Eligibility for Class A Executives
facts.sentence: Participation in the program is limited to employees designated by the employer as Class A Executives.

facts.name: Class A Executive Definition
facts.sentence: Class A Executives include individuals at Vice President level and above.

facts.name: Eligibility Start Date
facts.sentence: Eligibility can begin either at the time of policy issuance or upon subsequent written designation by the employer.

facts.name: Employer Discretion in Enrollment
facts.sentence: The employer retains sole discretion to add employees to the eligible class.

facts.name: Employer Discretion in Removal
facts.sentence: The employer retains sole discretion to remove employees from the eligible class.

facts.name: EOI Requirement Above Limit
facts.sentence: Addition to the eligible class requires Evidence of Insurability (EOI) if the employee is classified above the Guaranteed Issue Limit.

facts.name: Eligibility Start Date
facts.sentence: Eligibility commences on the date of written designation by the employer.

facts.name: Pinnacle Acceptance Requirement
facts.sentence: Eligibility also depends on Pinnacle's written acceptance.

facts.name: Death Benefit Formula
facts.sentence: Total death benefit equals five times total annual compensation.

facts.name: Compensation Definition
facts.sentence: Total annual compensation is defined as base salary plus target annual cash bonus.

facts.name: Compensation Measurement Date
facts.sentence: Total annual compensation is measured as of January 1 of the coverage year.

facts.name: Annual Benefit Recalibration
facts.sentence: Benefit is recalculated annually on March 1.

facts.name: Annual Benefit Recalibration Timing
facts.sentence: The recalculated benefit uses compensation data as of the preceding January 1.

facts.name: Annual Compensation Certification Deadline
facts.sentence: The employer certifies compensation figures to Pinnacle by February 1 each year.

facts.name: Guaranteed Issue Limit
facts.sentence: Coverage up to $1,500,000 per executive is available without Evidence of Insurability (EOI) at initial enrollment.

facts.name: Guaranteed Issue Up to $1.5M
facts.sentence: Coverage up to $1,500,000 per executive is available without EOI at annual recalculation.

facts.name: Above $1.5M EOI Requirement
facts.sentence: Coverage above $1,500,000 per executive requires full Evidence of Insurability (EOI).

facts.name: Full EOI Requires Medical Exam
facts.sentence: Full EOI includes a medical examination.

facts.name: Max Death Benefit Cap
facts.sentence: Maximum death benefit per covered executive is $5,000,000.

facts.name: Employer Collateral Interest Calculation
facts.sentence: The employer’s collateral interest under the split-dollar endorsement equals the greater of two amounts: (a) cumulative premiums paid, or (b) 60% of the total death benefit.

facts.name: Employee Personal Benefit Calculation
facts.sentence: The employee’s personal benefit is the remaining portion of the death benefit after accounting for the employer’s collateral interest.

facts.name: Minimum Employee Benefit Share
facts.sentence: The minimum percentage allocated to the employee’s personal benefit is 40%.

facts.name: Collateral Assignment to FinServ
facts.sentence: The insured has collaterally assigned to FinServ Capital Group that portion

facts.name: Collateral Assignment of Employer Interest
facts.sentence: The insured has collaterally assigned to FinServ Capital Group the portion of the death benefit equal to the employer's interest.

facts.name: Employer Interest Definition Reference
facts.sentence: The employer's interest is defined in Section 3.5.

facts.name: Death Benefit Payment to Employer
facts.sentence: In the event of the insured's death, Pinnacle will pay the employer's portion of the death benefit directly to FinServ Capital Group.

facts.name: Death Benefit Distribution
facts.sentence: In the event of the insured's death, Pinnacle will pay the employee's personal benefit to the designated personal beneficiary.

facts.name: Employer Assignment Limitation
facts.sentence: The employer may not increase the collateral assignment percentage during the insured's lifetime.

facts.name: Collateral Assignment Consent Rule
facts.sentence: Any increase in the collateral assignment percentage requires the insured's written consent.

facts.name: Personal Benefit Assignment Restriction
facts.sentence: The employee may not assign the personal benefit portion without Pinnacle's written consent.

facts.name: Pledge Restriction on Personal Benefit
facts.sentence: The employee may not pledge the personal benefit portion without Pinnacle's written consent.

facts.name: Encumbrance Restriction on Personal Benefit
facts.sentence: The employee may not encumber the personal benefit portion without Pinnacle's written consent.

facts.name: Personal Benefit Vesting Threshold
facts.sentence: The employee's personal benefit vests at 20% if they have less than 2 years of Class A service.

facts.name: Vesting at 40% for 2–4 Years
facts.sentence: The employee's personal benefit vests at 40% if they have 2 but less than 4 years of Class A service.

facts.name: Vesting at 60% for 4–6 Years
facts.sentence: The employee's personal benefit vests at 60% if they have 4 but less than 6 years of Class A service.

facts.name: Vesting at 80% for 6–8 Years
facts.sentence: The employee's personal benefit vests at 80% if they have 6 but less than 8 years of Class A service.

facts.name: Full Vesting After 8 Years
facts.sentence: The employee's personal benefit vests at 100% if they have 8 or more years of Class A service.

facts.name: Non-Vested Benefits Revert to Employer
facts.sentence: Upon termination of employment before full vesting, the non-vested portion of the personal benefit reverts to the employer's collateral interest.

facts.name: Death-triggered vesting acceleration
facts.sentence: Vesting is immediately accelerated to 100% upon the death of the employee while covered.

facts.name: Vesting Acceleration Due to Disability
facts.sentence: Vesting is immediately accelerated to 100% upon total disability of the employee as defined in Section 9.

facts.name: Change-in-Control Vesting Trigger
facts.sentence: Vesting is immediately accelerated to 100% upon change in control of FinServ Capital Group.

facts.name: Immediate Vesting on Without Cause Termination
facts.sentence: Vesting is immediately accelerated to 100% upon termination of the employee by the employer without cause.

facts.name: Voluntary Resignation Assumption
facts.sentence: Upon voluntary resignation, the employee may assume the policy directly through an assume-and-assign process.

facts.name: Policy Assumption via Premium Payment
facts.sentence: To assume the policy directly, the employee must pay Pinnacle directly for premiums.

facts.name: Policy Assumption Triggers Termination
facts.sentence: When the employee assumes the policy directly, the split-dollar arrangement terminates.

facts.name: Policy Assumption Releases Employer Interest
facts.sentence: When the employee assumes the policy directly, the employer's collateral interest is released.

facts.name: Voluntary Resignation & Policy Assumption
facts.sentence: An employee may voluntarily resign and assume the policy directly by paying Pinnacle directly for premiums.

facts.name: Policy Assumption Ends Split-Dollar Arrangement
facts.sentence: Upon assuming the policy directly, the split-dollar arrangement terminates.

facts.name: Repayment releases collateral interest
facts.sentence: The employer's collateral interest is released upon repayment of cumulative employer premium advances.

facts.name: Unrepaid Premium Retention
facts.sentence: If the employer premium advance is not repaid, the employer retains its collateral interest.

facts.name: Non-Repayment Policy Conversion
facts.sentence: If the employer premium advance is not repaid, the policy converts to a personally owned individual term policy.

facts.name: Converted Policy Underwriting
facts.sentence: The converted individual term policy is subject to Pinnacle's then-current underwriting.

facts.name: Mandatory Policy Conversion Timeline
facts.sentence: Mandatory conversion to an individual policy is required within 60 days of termination.

facts.name: Group Coverage Termination Window
facts.sentence: Pinnacle will not continue group coverage beyond 60 days post-termination.

facts.name: Terminal Illness Benefit Acceleration
facts.sentence: Upon certification of terminal illness with a life expectancy of 12 months or less, the insured may accelerate up to 100% of the personal benefit portion.

facts.name: Employer Interest Exclusion from Acceleration
facts.sentence: The employer's collateral interest is not subject to acceleration.

facts.name: Maximum Acceleration Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum amount that can be accelerated is $500,000 or the full personal benefit, whichever is less.

facts.name: Actuarial Discount on Acceleration
facts.sentence: An actuarial discount applies to the accelerated payment.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Window
facts.sentence: No personal benefit is payable if death results from suicide within 24 months of the effective date of coverage.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion: Employer Benefit
facts.sentence: No employer collateral benefit is payable if death results from suicide within 24 months of the effective date of coverage.

facts.name: Contestability Period for Misrepresentation
facts.sentence: If the insured made a material misrepresentation in any application or EOI, Pinnacle may contest the claim within 2 years of the effective date of coverage.

facts.name: Policy Incontestability Post-Two Years
facts.sentence: After 2 years, the policy becomes incontestable except for fraudulent misrepresentation.

facts.name: No Pre-Existing Condition Exclusion
facts.sentence: There is no exclusion for pre-existing conditions.

facts.name: No Occupation Hazard Exclusion
facts.sentence: There is no exclusion for occupation hazards.

facts.name: Aviation Exclusion Exception
facts.sentence: There is no exclusion for aviation, other than licensed commercial scheduled service.

facts.name: Total Disability Definition
facts.sentence: Total disability means continuous inability to perform the material duties of the insured's own occupation as an executive.

facts.name: Duration Requirement for Total Disability
facts.sentence: Total disability requires a duration exceeding 180 days.

facts.name: Physician Certification Requirement
facts.sentence: Total disability must be certified by a physician.

facts.name: Total Disability Definition
facts.sentence: Total disability means continuous inability to perform the material duties of the insured's own occupation.

facts.name: Insured Occupation: Executive
facts.sentence: The insured's occupation is that of an executive.

facts.name: Duration of Total Disability
facts.sentence: A total disability must last for more than 180 days.

facts.name: Physician Certification Requirement
facts.sentence: Total disability must be certified by a board-certified physician.

facts.name: Employer Notification Deadline
facts.sentence: Upon the death of the insured, the employer must be notified within 30 days.

facts.name: Beneficiary Notification Timeline
facts.sentence: Upon the death of the insured, the personal beneficiary must be notified within 30 days.

facts.name: Claim Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: Pinnacle will issue claim payments to the employer within 10 business days of receiving complete documentation.

facts.name: Claim Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: Pinnacle will issue claim payments to the personal beneficiary within 10 business days of receiving complete documentation.

facts.name: Certified Death Certificate Requirement
facts.sentence: Complete documentation includes a certified death certificate.

facts.name: Required Claim Documentation
facts.sentence: Complete documentation includes a completed employer claim certification.

facts.name: Personal Beneficiary Claim Form Requirement
facts.sentence: Complete documentation includes a personal beneficiary claim form.

facts.name: Beneficiary Identity Proof Requirement
facts.sentence: Complete documentation includes identity proof from the personal beneficiary.

facts.name: Split-Dollar Release Documentation
facts.sentence: If applicable, complete documentation includes an employer written release for split-dollar release.

facts.name: Claim Submission Address
facts.sentence: Claim submissions must be sent to Pinnacle Life Assurance – Executive Claims Unit.

facts.name: Claims Mailing Address
facts.sentence: The mailing address for claims is One Financial Square, New York, NY 10005.

facts.name: Claims Contact Number
facts.sentence: The direct line for claims inquiries is 1-800-555-9100.

facts.name: Governing Law Jurisdiction
facts.sentence: This insurance certificate is governed by the laws of New York State.

facts.name: Issuer Identification
facts.sentence: The issuer of this certificate is Pinnacle Life Assurance Corporation.

facts.name: Corporate Location
facts.sentence: Pinnacle Life Assurance Corporation is located in New York, New York.

facts.name: Certificate Issuance Authority
facts.sentence: The certificate was issued by the Executive Vice President, Group Products.

facts.name: Certificate Issuance Date
facts.sentence: The certificate was issued on March 1, 2024.

facts.name: Spousal Eligibility Termination

facts.name: New Member Enrollment Window
facts.sentence: Members who join NAIFA are eligible to enroll within 60 days of joining.

facts.name: New Member Tier Enrollment
facts.sentence: New members within 60 days of joining NAIFA may enroll at any coverage tier up to Tier 4.

facts.name: New Member EOI Waiver

facts.name: Post-60-Day Enrollment EOI Requirement
facts.sentence: Enrollment after 60 days requires Evidence of Insurability (EOI) for any coverage tier.

facts.name: Annual Open Enrollment Period
facts.sentence: NAIFA conducts an annual 30-day open enrollment period each January.

facts.name: Open Enrollment Tier Increase
facts.sentence: During open enrollment, members may increase their coverage by one tier without EOI.

facts.name: Open Enrollment Tier Increase Requirement
facts.sentence: Increases of two or more tiers during open enrollment require Evidence of Insurability (EOI).

facts.name: Coverage Tier Selection
facts.sentence: Member coverage is elected in tiers ranging from Tier 1 to Tier 5.

facts.name: Tier 1 Benefit Amount
facts.sentence: Tier 1 provides a member benefit of $50,000.

facts.name: Tier 2 Benefit Amount
